title: Patatas Bravas
subtitle: Crisp fried potatoes with a fiery tomato and smoked paprika sauce
excerpt: Chunks of potato fried until golden and served with a punchy bravas sauce made from tinned tomatoes, smoked paprika and chilli.
sourceNotes: A classic Spanish tapas dish served in bars throughout the country.

recipe.batchNotes: The bravas sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days. Make a big batch and reheat as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made ahead and reheated. Fry the potatoes just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: The spicy tomato sauce served with fried potatoes in Spain, named for its fiery character.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 as a tapas dish and takes 45 minutes in total. The sauce takes about 15 minutes, and you can make it while the potatoes are frying. Everything comes together quickly once both are done.

The key to crisp potatoes is dry potatoes. After cutting them, pat the pieces very well with kitchen paper. Any surface moisture will steam rather than fry, leaving you with soft, pale results. Fry in a single layer in batches if necessary.

Make the sauce first. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 1 minute until golden. Add the smoked paprika and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.

Add the tinned tomatoes, season with black pepper and stir well. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick and deep red. Taste and adjust the heat with more chilli if you like. Keep warm over the lowest heat.
Pat the potato chunks very dry with kitchen paper. Heat 5 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat until shimmering.

Add the potatoes in a single layer, making sure there is space between each piece. Fry for 10 minutes without moving, then turn and fry for another 8 to 10 minutes until golden and crisp all over. Work in batches if needed.
Drain the potatoes briefly on kitchen paper. Pile into a warm serving dish, spoon the bravas sauce over the top and serve immediately.

items.problem: The potatoes are soggy rather than crisp
items.solution: They were not dried thoroughly enough or the pan was overcrowded. Fry in smaller batches with well-dried potatoes.

items.problem: The sauce is thin and watery
items.solution: Cook it for longer uncovered to let the liquid evaporate. It should coat the back of a spoon before you pour it over the potatoes.

items.problem: The sauce is too spicy to enjoy
items.solution: Start with a quarter teaspoon of chilli powder and taste as you go. Smoked paprika adds warmth without significant heat.

content.text: Patatas bravas is one of the most recognisable tapas dishes in Spain. The

sauce varies by region, with Madrid versions using a simple spiced tomato and Barcelona versions sometimes adding a garlic mayonnaise. This recipe sticks to the tomato version, which travels better and keeps its punch even when made ahead. Serve with cocktail sticks and cold beer.
